newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine may have 1 mln T wheat to export.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine may have 1 mln T wheat to export.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
DESPITE BAD HARVEST, UKRAINE MAY HAVE UP TO ONE MILLION TONNES OF WHEAT FOR EXPORT OVER 1996/97

MOSCOW, Dec 16 - Ukraine's total wheat output for 1996 is estimated to decline to a net 14 million tonnes. This compares with 1995's wheat harvest of 16.3 million tonnes, which was the lowest in 17 years.
Lower domestic consumption means Ukraine may be able to remain a grain exporter over the remainder of 1996 and 1997.
But state procurement problems could emerge as a major barrier to exports.
The state had planned to purchase about 4.55 million tonnes of grain for human consumption.
Regional procurements were planned at the same level, but have been revised down to three million tonnes.
However, the financing of grain procurements would require substantial, inflationary state credits.
Authorities, particularly regional administrations, have therefore taken a range of measures designed to restrict producers' ability to sell their output.

Although the government has said that there are no problems with exports and that legally there can be ban on exports, Ukrainian grain traders say the government continues to prevent deliveries abroad.

In fact, exports of grain and grain products are now officially possible only under contracts concluded on the commodities exchanges, which at present handle only five to 10 percent of the grain trade.
At the same time, regional administrations can enter the market as wheat exporters.
By the end of November, they had procured more than one million tonnes, mainly wheat.
Of this, about 30 to 35 percent may be exported on barter terms for fuel and machinery to other countries in the Commonwealth of Indepedent States.
Ukraine's wheat exports (not including wheat flour) from its 1996 harvest were 60,000 tonnes in September and 63,000 tonnes in October.
The bulk was delivered to CIS states (38,000 tonnes in September, 44,000 tonnes in October), particularly to Belarus and Turkmenistan under intergovernment agreements.
